questions.question: Why should charter bus passengers wait to board until departure time?

options.text: The bus costs money once the first passenger boards. Waiting saves money.
Passengers may get on and off multiple times and miss the departure.
Passengers cannot choose their seats until the bus is about to leave.
Waiting to board helps prevent theft and vandalism.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting to board helps prevent theft and vandalism.
questions.explanation: Charter bus drivers should not let passengers board until departure time. This helps prevent theft and vandalism.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a drawbridge with no signal light or traffic control attendant?

options.text: Continue across carefully.
Speed up to cross quickly.
Wait for another driver to cross first.
Stop and make sure the bridge is completely closed before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and make sure the bridge is completely closed before crossing.
questions.explanation: Always stop at any drawbridge without a signal light or traffic control attendant. Stop at least 50 feet before the bridge opening. Make sure the bridge is fully closed before you cross.

questions.question: What should a bus driver do if a passenger tries to board with a container of gasoline?

options.text: Place the container near the back of the bus.
Place the container near the front of the bus.
Place the container in the aisle.
Do not allow the container on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not allow the container on the bus.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must not allow passengers to bring hazards onto the bus, such as gasoline or car batteries.

questions.question: What should you do with access panels before driving?

options.text: Open them.
Remove them.
Store them inside the storage compartment.
Close them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close them.
questions.explanation: Before driving, inspect the outside of your bus. Close all emergency exits and access panels.

questions.question: Is a curve's posted design speed always safe for buses?

options.text: Yes, it is safe for buses.
Yes, it is safe for all vehicles, including buses.
It is the minimum speed you must drive.
No, it is not always safe for buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is not always safe for buses.
questions.explanation: A bus may roll over or slide off the road even at the posted design speed for a curve. Always reduce your speed when driving a bus around a curve.

questions.question: Where should carry-on bags be secured on a bus?

options.text: In front of the back door.
In front of the front door.
In a location that does not block any emergency exits.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a location that does not block any emergency exits.
questions.explanation: Passengers must not leave luggage in doorways or aisles. All items must be secured so passengers can exit through any door or window in an emergency.

questions.question: What should you check when inspecting the interior of a bus?

options.text: You do not need to look at handrails and floor lining.
Make sure the seats are loosely secured.
Assume all buzzers work properly.
Make sure emergency exits work and are easy to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure emergency exits work and are easy to use.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the interior, check that everything is safe and works properly. Make sure emergency exits are clearly marked and easy to use.

questions.question: How should a brake and accelerator interlock system be used?

options.text: Turn it off in most situations.
Use it only in bad weather.
Never use it instead of the parking brake.
Use it to operate the rear door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never use it instead of the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Some buses have a brake and accelerator interlock system that applies the brakes when the rear door is open. Do not use this system as a substitute for the parking brake.

questions.question: What is a standee line?

options.text: A line that passengers must stand behind.
A line that passengers must stand on.
A line used as passengers exit the bus.
A line on the outside of a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: A line that passengers must stand behind.
questions.explanation: On buses with standing passengers, no one may stand in front of the rear of the driver's seat. A standee line marks where passengers cannot stand.

questions.question: What should you do before driving a bus that has been parked for several days?

options.text: Assume the interior is in good condition.
Call the local police department.
Walk through the bus and check for any damage since the last trip.
Ask passengers to check the interior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus and check for any damage since the last trip.
questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged. Before driving a bus that has been parked, inspect the interior to make sure everything is in proper condition.

questions.question: What can buses never carry?

options.text: Tear gas.
Any amount of solid Class 6 poisons.
Bottled oxygen.
Emergency hospital supplies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tear gas.
questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry tear gas, poison gas, liquid Class 6 poisons, or irritating materials. Radioactive materials are also forbidden.

questions.question: What must a bus driver do regarding seat belts?

options.text: Does not need to wear a seat belt.
Must always wear a seat belt.
Must wear a seat belt, but only during usual school hours.
Must wear a seat belt, but only if they have been licensed for less than a year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must always wear a seat belt. The driver's seat must have a seat belt that the driver uses at all times.

questions.question: What should you check when inspecting the inside of a bus?

options.text: Assume all emergency exits work properly.
Loosen every seat.
Check all signaling devices.
Not waste time looking at the handrails and floor lining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all signaling devices.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the inside of a bus, check that all signaling devices work properly. This includes bathroom emergency buzzers and other alert systems.

questions.question: What must a bus driver's seat have?

options.text: A pocket for storage on its left side.
A pocket for storage on its right side.
A seat belt.
A cup holder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat belt.
questions.explanation: A bus driver's seat must have a seat belt. The driver should always use this seat belt.

questions.question: When should you remind passengers to take their carry-on bags when leaving the bus?

options.text: Before you stop the bus.
After you stop the bus.
At least five times.
As they exit the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you stop the bus.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to take their carry-on bags before you bring the bus to a complete stop at the destination.

questions.question: When should you sign a previous driver's vehicle inspection report?

options.text: The previous driver dated their entry.
Reported defects are certified to have been repaired.
You plan to drive for longer than one hour or travel farther than 50 miles.
The report is left on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reported defects are certified to have been repaired.
questions.explanation: Sign a previous inspection report only if the reported defects have been repaired or if no repairs were needed.

questions.question: What happens when you open the forward door at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Can increase your chances of hearing an approaching train.
Should never be done.
Could allow other noises to enter the bus, making it more difficult to hear any approaching trains.
Will take too long and is discouraged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can increase your chances of hearing an approaching train.
questions.explanation: Open the forward door at a railroad crossing if it helps you hear or see an approaching train better.

questions.question: What should a charter bus driver do?

options.text: Tell passengers how to operate the TVs, if equipped.
Not allow passengers to board until the scheduled departure time.
Allow passengers to board early to get ahead of schedule.
Tell passengers to fill the back of the bus first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allow passengers to board until the scheduled departure time.
questions.explanation: Do not let passengers board before the scheduled departure time. This helps prevent theft and damage to the bus.

questions.question: What should you check before driving a bus that was left unattended?

options.text: The vehicle should be thoroughly washed.
Air should be removed from tires.
The interior should be checked for damage.
The driver should look for any animals that may have gotten onboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: The interior should be checked for damage.
questions.explanation: Walk through the inside of the bus and check for any damage. Unattended buses can be damaged by people.

questions.question: What should you check when inspecting the inside of a bus?

options.text: Loosen every seat.
Check every handhold.
Assume all buzzers work properly.
Remove the emergency exit handles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check every handhold.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the inside of a bus, make sure every handhold and railing is secure and safe to use.
